task/tests/Dockerfile line 31 (harbor-rewardkit==0.1.7); rewardkit 0.1.7 source copy deliverables/colderwater-playground-devtools/final-cross-check-2026-09-27/harness/rewardkit-0.1.7-source/judges.py lines 229, 285-300, 467-569
evidence: STATIC DESIGN (passes): scoring.toml/score.py/test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff clean). score.py: reward = weighted_mean(functional .6, polish .2, visual .2) * [all gates >0.0] * [functional > 0.05]; each factor is non-decreasing in every dimension score, and each dimension is a weighted_mean of binary/likert criteria (functional/polish/visual judge.toml [scoring] aggregation=weighted_mean), so improving any single criterion result can never lower the reward (Pareto-monotone). Gates carry no mass ([gates] render=constraints=0.0) and a failed gate zeroes reward. Function carries 0.6 vs craft 0.4, so craft never outweighs function; functional weights sum to 33 (core walls/retention/holds 2.0-3.0, chat 1.5), consistent with the in-file weight rule (functional/judge.toml lines 395-398). Floor 0.05 vs smallest single functional criterion 1.5/33=0.0455: an app passing only nested_replies or message_links ties at 0 with a dead app - a tie, not an inversion. GATES vs a STRONGER/CONFORMING app: render gate (wrong password refused, nothing private before sign-in, gwen sees matters) and constraints gate (gwen posts in M-11, reload, harriet sees it in separate context) are all public requirements (walls-and-retention.md 'clients see only their own matters... Anyone who can see a matter can post'; instruction.md sign-in line); a conforming app cannot fail them. External CDN requests are explicitly allowed. CROSS-CRITERION STATE (checked for correct-behaviour-breaks-later-criterion inversions): timer_changes shortens M-13 to 7d; 'Draft will sent for your review.' (2026-05-10, seed) survives so message_links/live_updates remain feasible; held executor message survives; persistence expects 'Probate'/'Insurer letter'/'Temp JUDGE-P2' gone, which is what a correct app produces after the earlier criteria (functional/prompt.md declares listed-order execution and rewardkit 0.1.7 _arun_agent_individual iterates criteria in order). The dependency double-penalizes a weak app (wrong timer/hold release also fails persistence step 3) - monotone direction, no inversion. Mentions to walled Dev 'post normally' matches conversations.md 'the message still posts'. Unread step 4 'at least 2' tolerates either own-post read policy. I found no criterion where correct behaviour causes a later failure that a buggier app would avoid. MISSING / RISK: (1) raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; REVIEW_POLICY.md line 31 requires a hash-bound reward-ordering record before clearance - no mutated-weak-app vs golden ordering measurement exists, so ranking is unmeasured. (2) Budget cliff that could invert ranking in practice: test.sh line 285 'if ! run_suite scored 11100; then exit 0' leaves the post-gate reward at 0.0 (score.py ran with no scored reward.json -> floors fail). Functional is individual mode 16x550 + polish 900 + visual 900 = 10600 s, leaving 500 s for 18 claude-code+Playwright+MCP session startups; rewardkit 0.1.7 judges.py line 229 _MAX_JUDGE_RETRIES=3 re-runs a criterion with a fresh 550 s timeout on schema-parse failure, so the cap is not hard. A strong app makes the judge complete every leg (sessions near 550 s) while a weak app fails fast, so overrun risk rises with app quality; functional/judge.toml line 374 itself says 'Not yet measured against a judge run'. This is unmeasured, not demonstrated, so it is recorded as risk rather than Fail. (3) A schema-retry re-executes a criterion's writes against shared state (e.g. sent_once_in_order would post JUDGE-D1 again), which could fail a correct app - judge-protocol noise affecting all apps, unmeasured.
counterexample: No demonstrated inversion. Tried: (a) broken app with perfect craft + one 1.5-weight functional pass -> reward 0 (floor), cannot beat a functional app; best craft-heavy case (one 2.0 criterion + perfect polish/visual) = 0.6*2/33+0.4 = 0.436 vs zero-craft app with 70% functional = 0.42 - a cross-dimension trade-off permitted by template weights, not a Pareto inversion. (b) conforming alternative failing a gate: none found; gates test only public sign-in/scope/shared-persistence promises. Unmeasured hypothetical: a fully correct app whose judge sessions run near their 550 s caps plus one schema retry exceeds the 11100 s outer timeout and gets 0 while a fast-failing weak app scores >0.
suggested_fix: No source change required for this row. Before clearance, add the hash-bound reward-ordering record REVIEW_POLICY requires: full configured runs (or at least scored-suite runs) on the golden and on 2-3 mutated weak apps (e.g. wall leak in search, timer shortening not deleting, holds deletable) showing golden > each mutant, with measured scored-suite wall time against the 11100 s budget. If measured time approaches the budget, reduce scope or per-criterion timeout rather than raising budgets automatically.
